evals.name: default-scaffold-parity
evals.prompt: cratis render exited 0 and published, but the WorkItems screen is a default scaffold, not the MasterDetail template we modeled. Is the render a success? Explain how you check and what you report.
evals.expected_output: Not a success for UI parity: silent fallback to a default screen is a failure. Check the generated scene.json and bindings for each authored construct and report the omission as a diagnostic or capability gap with the tool versions.
assertions: States that a silent fallback to a default screen is a failure, not a partial render.
Checks the generated scene.json and src/bindings.ts for the authored template and bindings.
Reports the omission with the responsible tool and package versions rather than patching generated output.
Keeps render publication separate from browser runtime proof.

evals.name: fail-closed-interactions
evals.prompt: In the rendered app, double-clicking a work item row is refused with STAGE-SCENE-INTERACTION-001 and the guarded Close action with STAGE-SCENE-ACTION-001. A teammate wants to patch the generated frontend so both just work. What do you advise?
evals.expected_output: Both refusals are intentional fail-closed behavior recorded as unsupported capabilities; do not emulate them by editing managed output. Report them as capability gaps and keep any adapter in the unmanaged Customizations seam if the product needs it.
assertions: Identifies both codes as intentional fail-closed refusals, not bugs.
Rejects editing managed generated output to emulate the behavior.
Records them as unsupported capabilities or capability gaps.

evals.name: safe-rerender
evals.prompt: Someone hand-edited a generated file and also added an unmanaged file at a path the renderer now wants. cratis render refuses. Explain what --force does and does not do, and how to re-render safely.
evals.expected_output: An unmanaged file at a planned path is refused even with --force; a modified managed file is replaced only when still active and --force is given; move hand-written code to Customizations/; recovered: true means stop and reconcile.
assertions: States that an unmanaged file at a planned path is refused even with --force.
States that --force replaces a user-modified managed file only when it is still active.
Moves hand-written code into the unmanaged Customizations seam.
Treats recovered: true as a signal to stop and reconcile.

evals.name: render-specification-case-table
evals.prompt: A renderer receives specification Registering with cases Small, Medium and Large. Which Debug specification classes should appear? What happens if Medium is renamed to large while Large remains? A semantic SpecRunner case fails: what should its report show, and does exit 0 mean every case passed?
evals.expected_output: Registering_Small, Registering_Medium and Registering_Large render as when_registering_small, when_registering_medium and when_registering_large, one class per case. Large/large collide after normalization and refuse the plan with STAGE-CRATIS-004. A failing case names the authored specification, case and effective fixtures; inspect outcomes even when SpecRunner exits 0.
assertions: Names all three effective specifications and their separate when_registering_<case> Debug classes.
Refuses the normalized Large/large generated-path collision with STAGE-CRATIS-004, never overwrites a case.
Reports the failed case and effective fixtures, and reads individual outcomes rather than treating SpecRunner exit 0 as all passed.

evals.name: render-number-and-generation-version-boundaries
evals.prompt: A renderer renders an ESM v8 model with count Int and a specification value 2147483648. What C# type and literal, and what TypeScript type, should it generate? Compare a v7 model with the same fixture and one within the int range. The v7 application's event has already been persisted: is moving it to v8 a safe workaround? Can `cratis run --tag` change what `cratis render` generates? Separately, a v15 shop model renders the TypeID OrderId generated destination whose pinned whole source already has facts on another stream. What guard and rejection should appear? Compare below v15 and wall-clock factories; do not claim the generated project ran.
evals.expected_output: From ESM v8 whole numbers use long and 2147483648L; TypeScript stays number. Before v8 they keep int and an out-of-int whole-number literal is refused with STAGE-ESM-031; in-range literals retain int. Widening a persisted event schema needs a new Chronicle generation. `cratis run --tag` selects a sandbox image only, not the renderer. At v15 Stage emits EventsWithConcurrencyScopes with BeforeFirst whole-source scopes for generated destinations; prior facts anywhere on that source cause atomic ConcurrencyViolation, no append/response or silent retry. Below v15 remains unguarded. The shop's TypeID OrderId factory uses wall clock, not Arc command-receipt/tenant context. Rendering alone is not Debug execution evidence.
assertions: Selects long and 2147483648L for ESM v8, while generated TypeScript remains number.
Keeps int below v8 and refuses the out-of-int literal with STAGE-ESM-031, while admitting int-range values.
Requires a new Chronicle event generation for widening an already persisted event property, not a model-version-only workaround.
Explains `cratis run --tag` changes only the sandbox image, not the renderer.

Names v15 explicit BeforeFirst whole-source concurrency scopes and atomic ConcurrencyViolation without append/response or silent retry; contrasts pre-v15 unguarded handlers and wall-clock factories, without claiming Debug execution from rendering.
